title: The House That Was Waiting
summary: At Hushwater, Maela Crow recognizes Brandon as Andrew Keane and produces a sealed packet she has been holding for Andrew. Because Raina and Samuel have remained with the group since the Long Mile, neither could have primed Hushwater during the current approach; the older provenance still has to be established.

panelPlan.text: Hushwater is a modest settlement of shaded houses and a communal dining court, with no obvious Sunforge in the immediate center.
Maela sees Brandon, says 'Andrew Keane' with tired relief rather than shock, and goes inside before he can correct her.

Maela returns with a visibly old sealed cloth packet marked for ANDREW KEANE. Its age proves only that Andrew's story predates the group; it does not yet prove when anyone connected Brandon to Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Don't start. I've been waiting since winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That's a long time to wait for the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Who told you he was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Woman passing through. Green scarf. Shaved on the left side.

directionInline.text: Do not use the packet's age as the causal proof. The packet establishes a real preexisting Andrew story. The dated household record of the later traveler, examined on Page 3, is what places the Brandon-specific prediction before Raina's operation.

title: The Promise in the Packet
summary: Maela explains that a dying friend asked her to hold the packet for Andrew Keane and that a later traveler described Brandon's appearance closely enough that she believed the promise finally had an endpoint.

panelPlan.text: Maela sets the packet between herself and Brandon but does not force it into his hands.
She explains that her friend Lysa died believing Andrew would come. Months later another traveler gave a description matching Brandon.
Brandon refuses to open the packet because it is addressed to someone else, frustrating Maela without disrespecting her promise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa gave me this for Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Do you? The traveler described your face, your coat, even the way you stand near a door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Because his name is on it.

directionInline.text: Keep the packet human and morally specific, not a glowing mystery artifact. Its contents do not need to be revealed to prove the larger causal problem.

title: Before Raina
summary: Raina reconstructs the dates from Maela's household ledger. The ledger records the later traveler who described a man matching Brandon and linked him to Andrew; that visit predates Raina first learning Brandon's name and predates Samuel joining her. The explanation exposed in Issue 4 cannot have caused this setup.

panelPlan.text: Raina lays her own dated notes beside Maela's household ledger. The relevant entry records the winter visitor, the Andrew name and enough of the description to show that the Brandon-specific prediction existed before Raina's case did.
Samuel asks for the traveler's description. Maela remembers a woman with a shaved left temple and a green scarf, nobody Samuel recognizes.
Eva watches Raina try every ordinary explanation before finally accepting the chronology.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Could the Last Drop story have doubled back?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: If it helps, I remember being annoyed the same day.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Good. I was worried you'd wasted my irritation.

directionInline.text: The causal proof is documentary chronology, not mystical certainty: Maela's ledger dates the Brandon-like description and Andrew expectation before Raina knew Brandon's name. This falsifies Raina/Samuel as the source of this particular setup while leaving ordinary unknown intermediaries possible.

title: We Know Him
summary: Eva and Jessie no longer reopen the possibility that Brandon is secretly Andrew. Their months of ordinary life with him have made the identity question emotionally obsolete even while the external mystery deepens.

panelPlan.text: Outside Maela's house, Eva, Jessie, Raina and Samuel argue over provenance while Brandon sits apart mending a strap.
Raina asks whether they can truly exclude Brandon having some unknown connection to Andrew. Eva answers before Brandon does.
Jessie backs her, not from theory but from accumulated knowledge of the person traveling with them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: We still have to ask whether he knows Andrew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: No. I don't think we do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: You don't know every year of his life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He can surprise us. He probably will. But he's Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Then Andrew is the interesting part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I preferred being the boring part.

directionInline.text: This is the character payoff: the audience is invited to stop treating Brandon as a locked box. The mystery moves outward.

title: What the Promise Belongs To
summary: Brandon helps Maela separate her promise to Lysa from the mistaken belief that he is Andrew. Maela decides to keep the packet rather than force closure through the wrong man.

panelPlan.text: Maela admits she wanted Brandon to be Andrew because it would release her from carrying the promise.
Brandon tells her he cannot release her, but that keeping a promise does not require pretending the wrong person fulfilled it.
Samuel watches Brandon do pastoral work without naming it and understands why communities keep making use of him even when the assigned identity is false.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I wanted you to be him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Then I could be finished with this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa died believing he'd come. I promised her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So what am I supposed to do with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: The preacher would have something better.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I am trying very hard not to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I only know I'm not Andrew. Opening it for me won't make your promise complete.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So I still have to decide.

directionInline.text: Brandon's humanity, not hidden identity, is what makes him useful. Samuel should recognize the contrast with his own manipulative use of people's needs.

title: The Question Moves
summary: The group leaves Hushwater with the first arc's human conspiracy definitively demoted from cause to interference. Eva states the new question: not who Brandon is, but why people and stories keep arriving before him.

panelPlan.text: Maela remains at her doorway with the sealed packet, choosing not to manufacture closure.
The five travelers move out together; Raina and Samuel are now plainly members of the moving group rather than agents positioned ahead and behind.
On the road, Eva closes the old page in her notebook labeled WHO IS BRANDON? and starts a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The page that says 'Who is Brandon?'

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: What did you put in its place?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I know the question. I don't know how to write it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why do people keep getting a version of him before he gets there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I still don't particularly need the answer.

directionInline.text: This is Worldview Reset #3. Raina and Samuel are fellow witnesses now. Do not answer what lies behind the pattern; change the question cleanly.
